name: Vegetable Lo Mein
steps: Boil the eggless wheat noodles in plenty of water until just tender according to the pack, usually 4–6 minutes. Drain and rinse briefly with cool water to stop cooking. Shake dry well; wet noodles will dilute the sauce.

Whisk light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, sugar, rice vinegar and the measured 40 ml water until the sugar dissolves. Wash the bok choy thoroughly, especially between the stems, and separate large leaves. Slice all remaining vegetables before starting the stir-fry.

Heat the neutral oil in a large wok over high heat. Add garlic, shiitake mushrooms and the white parts of the spring onion; stir-fry 2 minutes until the mushrooms begin to brown. Add carrot and bell pepper and toss another 2 minutes.

Add bok choy stems for 1 minute, then the leaves and cook until they just wilt. Add the drained noodles. Pour the mixed sauce around the hot pan, lifting and folding the noodles for 2–3 minutes until the colour is even and most liquid has evaporated.
Turn off the heat when the noodles are glossy but not soggy. Scatter over the green spring onion and sesame seeds. Divide immediately into four bowls so the vegetables retain some bite.
tips: Use labelled egg-free noodles; many packaged lo mein noodles contain egg. The reviewed photo shows medium-thick glossy wheat noodles with shiitake, bok choy, carrot, red pepper, scallion and sesame.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
